items.name: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
items.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
items.description: Recent work on robot manipulation has focused on specialist policies trained on demonstrations. We show that generalist AI models can control manipulators more reliably than specialist policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs). We systematically analyze agentic manipulation policies (AMPs), in which a generalist AI model commands the manipulator directly, adapting its actions as the task unfolds. items.title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
items.description: Large language models reinvent the wheel all the time. They conflate task-solving with the execution of the solutions, which forces them to solve every problem from scratch. We show that once a task has been reasoned through, the application of its solution to a new problem instance can be done very efficiently and with little involvement from language models. items.title: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks
items.description: We prove that the set $\mathcal{N}_N$ of ReLU networks with one hidden layer and at most $N\in\mathbb N$ neurons is weakly closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$, for a bounded connected open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$. Consequently, every coercive, weakly lower semicontinuous energy on this space attains its minimum over $\mathcal{N}_N$. items.title: FlowMoP: Stochastic Multi-Person Motion Prediction
items.description: Predicting the future motion of multiple people is inherently stochastic: the same observed history admits many plausible continuations depending on intent, coordination, and social context. items.name: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
items.title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Test-time reinforcement learning (TTRL) adapts pretrained language models to unlabeled target-domain data using self-generated pseudo-labels, whose reliability remains poorly understood. We analyze majority-vote supervision for TTRL with online Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and decompose its error into population-majority bias and prompt-dependent finite-rollout variation. items.title: GRAC: Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning for Surgical Scene Description
items.description: Purpose: Surgical operative reports support procedural documentation, surgical training, performance assessment, and workflow review. items.description: Can a sender that only computes hashes, with a language model only at the receiver, transmit short human text more cheaply than a classical sender trained on the same domain? items.name: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists
items.title: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists
items.description: In many areas of AI, general-purpose models have increasingly replaced handcrafted methods and specialized architectures. We argue that embodied AI is poised for a similar shift. Our key claim is that embodied tasks can be formulated as interaction with digital software. Specifically, we build software that renders an agent's view of a physical environment on a screen and provides controls for acting in it. items.title: Ensemble Methodology for Reference-Free Confidence Estimation in LLM-based Code Summarization
items.description: This paper describes an approach and use case to estimate the correctness of LLM-generated COBOL summaries without access to human-authored references. items.title: Can Agentic Systems Close the Gap in Radiology with Production AI Tools?
items.description: Radiology AI has developed along two paths: specialized models that perform well on narrow tasks but cover few clinical findings, and generalist models that address a broader range of tasks but remain prone to hallucination and inaccurate measurements. items.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) rewards are notoriously difficult to design and control, often leading to the model learning unintended behaviors such as reward hacking. items.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
items.description: The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. items.name: Machine learning for lattice QCD
items.title: Machine learning for lattice QCD
items.description: Machine learning (ML) methods have been explored as a means of optimizing lattice field theory calculations, with increasing interest in recent years. This chapter gives an introduction and summary to the use of ML methods to optimize lattice field theory without introducing any uncontrolled approximations.
